examples.why: リンクから使用できます is a calque; a native technical writer would write 利用できます (or 以下のリンクにあります) for resources reachable via a link.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — statuses (QUEUED/INITIALIZING/RUNNING/DONE), the `@distribute_task(target={"cpu": 1})` explanation, the 16 CPU cores / 32 GB RAM figure, the 1024-byte chain and the `/data` flat-storage limitations all match the English exactly, and register is consistent desu/masu with no keigo. Two small editorial slips, neither misleading: (1) in the "Explore different task configurations" section the forward pointer "as shown in the following" is dropped from the CPU-core sentence (「…割り当てることができます。」 with no 以下に示すように), so the sentence no longer points the reader at the code cell that demonstrates fractional allocation; (2) two inline link labels are left in English inside otherwise Japanese prose — 「[Write your first Qiskit Serverless program](/guides/serverless-first-program)のトピック」 and 「[Upload to Qiskit Serverless](...)を参照してください」 — where the surrounding text (e.g. 「[既存のコードをQiskit Serverlessに移植する]」 in Next steps) does translate link labels, so the file is internally inconsistent on this. Terminology is otherwise sound and consistent (transpile→トランスパイル/トランスパイレーション, classical resources→クラシカルリソース, worker→ワーカー, decorator→デコレーター).

examples.source: CPU cores can be allocated as full CPU cores, or even fractional allocations, as shown in the following.
examples.suggested: CPUコアは、以下に示すように、コア単位でも小数単位（部分割り当て）でも割り当てることができます。
examples.translation: CPUコアは、完全なCPUコアとして、またはフラクショナル割り当て（部分割り当て）として割り当てることができます。
examples.why: The qualifier "as shown in the following" is dropped, removing the pointer to the code cell that demonstrates the allocation; a dropped qualifier, not a meaning inversion.

examples.source: the [Write your first Qiskit Serverless program](/guides/serverless-first-program) topic ... (see [Upload to Qiskit Serverless](...) for instructions)
examples.suggested: [初めてのQiskit Serverlessプログラムを書く](...)のトピック ... （手順については[Qiskit Serverlessへのアップロード](...)を参照してください）
examples.translation: [Write your first Qiskit Serverless program](/guides/serverless-first-program)のトピック ... （手順については[Upload to Qiskit Serverless](...)を参照してください）
examples.why: These two link labels stay in English while the Next-steps link 「既存のコードをQiskit Serverlessに移植する」 is translated — inconsistent handling of cross-reference labels within the same file.

editor_note: Faithful paragraph-for-paragraph with no drift; core terms are correct and consistent (output register→出力レジスター, error suppression→エラー抑制, dynamical decoupling→ダイナミカル・デカップリング, ISA→命令セット・アーキテクチャー（ISA）回路, PUB→プリミティブ統合ブロック（PUB）タプル), the respectively-mapping in step 3 (バッチ、Session、ジョブ実行モード → batch/session/backend) and the Open Plan session-job caveat are both preserved, and the register stays plain desu/masu (お勧めします、参照してください) with no keigo.

Semantically faithful throughout — I checked the drift-prone passages one by one and all hold: the promise/goal framing ("Temos a *promessa* de que |ψ⟩ é um autovetor"), the non-distinctness caveat in Example 1 ("o teorema não diz que os números complexos ... são distintos"), the no-freedom-in-eigenvalues claim ("não há nenhuma liberdade na escolha dos autovalores, exceto quanto à sua ordenação"), the counter-clockwise wrap-around remark and the θ = 0,999 within-1/1000 example (correct pt decimal comma). Domain terminology is correct and consistent: autovalor/autovetor, matrizes normais/unitárias/Hermitianas, decomposição espectral, círculo unitário, transposta conjugada, norma Euclidiana, qubits kept in English. The only things a native technical editor would touch are two stiff literal renderings: "com entradas de números complexos" (calque of "complex number entries"; pt would write "com entradas complexas") and "muito útil de considerar" (the "de" before the infinitive is an English-shaped calque; native phrasing is "muito útil considerar"). Neither misleads.

examples.source: A square matrix $M$ with complex number entries is said to be a *normal* matrix if it commutes with its conjugate transpose
examples.suggested: Uma matriz quadrada $M$ com entradas complexas é dita *normal* se comuta com sua transposta conjugada
examples.translation: Uma matriz quadrada $M$ com entradas de números complexos é dita *normal* se ela comuta com sua transposta conjugada
examples.why: "entradas de números complexos" is a word-for-word rendering of "complex number entries"; standard Portuguese linear-algebra usage is "entradas complexas" (or "cujas entradas são números complexos"). Meaning is intact, only the phrasing is translationese.

examples.source: (This is a simple but great example of a matrix that's often very helpful to consider.)
examples.suggested: (Este é um exemplo simples, mas excelente, de uma matriz que costuma ser muito útil considerar.)
examples.translation: (Este é um exemplo simples, mas excelente, de uma matriz que costuma ser muito útil de considerar.)
examples.why: "útil de considerar" inserts a preposition Portuguese does not take in this impersonal construction — a calque of the English infinitive. A native technical writer would drop the "de" or recast as "que vale muito a pena considerar".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the delicate passages all survive intact: the non-commuting-operators argument, "Um passo de tempo menor leva a uma aproximação mais precisa… circuitos mais profundos… maior acumulação de erros", and the whole ↓↑/↑↓ spin-swap paragraph (transversal α=0° → troca de spin; longitudinal α=±90° → sem evolução; ±45° → troca mais provável com 67%) matches the English exactly, including the right-to-left label caveat. The defects are editorial, not misleading. (1) "gate" is rendered inconsistently: the prose says "portas quânticas"/"portas de dois qubits" everywhere in sections 1–2, but the two exercise instructions switch to the raw English "conte o número de gates" (3.1 and the fourth-order section). (2) "an array of spins" became "uma matriz de spins" — a programming calque of "array" that lands badly in a document where "matrizes de Pauli" appear two paragraphs later; "um arranjo/conjunto de spins" is what a native writer would put. (3) Small stiffness elsewhere: "uma representação esparsa de um operador em termos de termos de Pauli ponderados" (em termos de termos), the section-2.1 lead drops the "campo" from transverse-field ("o modelo de Ising transversal em 1D" vs the heading's "Ising com campo transversal"), and "down-up" is literalized as "baixo-cima" instead of "para baixo–para cima".

examples.source: Also, count the number of gates and depth of the circuit and compare with Lie–Trotter.
examples.suggested: Além disso, conte o número de portas e a profundidade do circuito e compare com o Lie–Trotter.
examples.translation: Além disso, conte o número de gates e a profundidade do circuito e compare com o Lie–Trotter.
examples.why: The rest of the file consistently uses "portas (quânticas)" — e.g. "as portas de dois qubits têm taxas de erro mais altas do que as portas de um qubit" (l. 229). Only the two exercise instructions switch to English "gates", splitting the term within the file.

examples.source: These lattices consist of an array of spins $\sigma_i$ that interact only with their nearest neighbors.
examples.suggested: Essas redes consistem em um arranjo de spins $\sigma_i$ que interagem apenas com seus vizinhos mais próximos.
examples.translation: Essas redes consistem em uma matriz de spins $\sigma_i$ que interagem apenas com seus vizinhos mais próximos.
examples.why: "array" → "matriz" is a programming calque; here it collides with the Pauli "matrizes" discussed nearby. The lattice is a 1-D arrangement of sites, not a matrix.

examples.source: A SparsePauliOp is a sparse representation of an operator in terms of weighted Pauli terms.
examples.suggested: Um SparsePauliOp é uma representação esparsa de um operador como uma soma ponderada de termos de Pauli.
examples.translation: Um SparsePauliOp é uma representação esparsa de um operador em termos de termos de Pauli ponderados.
examples.why: "em termos de termos" is an accidental echo no native technical writer would leave; rephrasing keeps the meaning and removes the stutter.

examples.source: We here consider the 1-D transverse-field Ising model.
examples.suggested: Aqui consideramos o modelo de Ising unidimensional com campo transversal.
examples.translation: Aqui consideramos o modelo de Ising transversal em 1D.
examples.why: Drops "campo": it is the field that is transverse, not the model. The section heading directly above already uses the full "Ising com campo transversal", so the shortened form also reads as an inconsistency.

examples.source: The initial spin configuration will be "down-up"
examples.suggested: A configuração inicial de spins será "para baixo–para cima" (↓↑)
examples.translation: A configuração inicial de spin será "baixo-cima"
examples.why: "baixo-cima" is a word-for-word literalization; Portuguese describes spin orientation as "para baixo / para cima". Not misleading (the ↓↑ arrows appear in the adjacent code comment) but visibly translated.

editor_note: Overall faithful and readable, with correct core terminology (estado fundamental, pacote de onda, condensado quiral, platôs estéreis, vidro de spin de Ising, mitigação e supressão de erros) and a consistent informal "você". Five things a native technical editor would change. (1) A hedge is dropped in the BF-DCQO paragraph: "reported on over 100 qubits for one of the first times" becomes "reportados em mais de 100 qubits pela primeira vez", turning "one of the first times" into an outright priority claim — it does not teach a false concept, but it overstates the source. (2) "colindo partículas" is a misspelling of "colidindo" in the LHC paragraph. (3) "agreement between theory and data" is calqued as "acordo muito bom entre a teoria e os dados"; the domain term is "concordância" ("acordo" reads as a negotiated agreement). (4) "expectation value" is rendered as "valor de expectativa" (twice, in the bias-field paragraph) where the conventional Portuguese physics term is "valor esperado"/"valor médio" — recognizable but calqued. (5) Same sentence carries the English "search … for" structure ("pesquisar o espaço de parâmetros multidimensional para o conjunto de parâmetros"), which a native writer would phrase as "vasculhar … em busca do conjunto de parâmetros". None of these would mislead a learner about the physics.

examples.source: good results are being reported on over 100 qubits for one of the first times.
examples.suggested: bons resultados estão sendo reportados em mais de 100 qubits, uma das primeiras vezes que isso acontece.
examples.translation: bons resultados estão sendo reportados em mais de 100 qubits pela primeira vez.
examples.why: The English hedges ("one of the first times"); the Portuguese asserts outright priority ("pela primeira vez"), a strengthened claim the source does not make.

examples.source: the LHC was built to enable the study of fundamental physics by colliding particles at super high energies
examples.suggested: ... colidindo partículas em energias altíssimas
examples.translation: o LHC foi construído para permitir o estudo da física fundamental colindo partículas em energias super altas
examples.why: "colindo" is not a Portuguese word — a misspelling of "colidindo"; "energias super altas" also reads better as "energias altíssimas".

examples.source: you can still obviously see very good agreement between theory and data
examples.suggested: você ainda vê claramente uma concordância muito boa entre teoria e dados
examples.translation: você ainda pode ver um acordo muito bom entre a teoria e os dados
examples.why: "agreement" between theory and measurement is "concordância" in Portuguese physics writing; "acordo" is a calque suggesting a negotiated agreement. The English "obviously" is also dropped.

examples.source: use classical optimizers to search the many-dimensional parameter space for the set of parameters that yields a minimum expectation value for a fixed Hamiltonian
examples.suggested: usam otimizadores clássicos para vasculhar o espaço de parâmetros multidimensional em busca do conjunto de parâmetros que produz o menor valor esperado para um Hamiltoniano fixo
examples.translation: usam otimizadores clássicos para pesquisar o espaço de parâmetros multidimensional para o conjunto de parâmetros que produz um valor de expectativa mínimo para um Hamiltoniano fixo
examples.why: "valor de expectativa" is a calque of "expectation value" (conventional term: "valor esperado"), and "pesquisar … para o conjunto" carries English "search … for" syntax that no native technical writer would use.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or hallucinated claims; the quantum-utility vs quantum-advantage distinction, the wind-tunnel analogy, and the three scale/quality/speed metrics all land correctly, and core terms are consistent and conventional ("portas de 2 qubits", "entrelaçamento", "mitigação de erros", "tolerantes a falhas", jobs/Qiskit Runtime kept in English). The defects are calque and grammar, not meaning. The recurring one is "quantum mechanical" split into two adjectives: "sistemas quânticos mecânicos" (twice, §Simulando a Natureza and §Computação quântica na teoria) and "descrição quântica mecânica do mundo" — Portuguese needs "sistemas da mecânica quântica" / "descrição do mundo pela mecânica quântica"; note the same file renders it correctly as plain "sistemas quânticos" one line later, so it is also internally inconsistent. Smaller slips: "an impossibly difficult problem" flattened to the stronger "um problema impossível"; the untranslated noun in "elevando física e tecnologia computacional pelos próprios bootstraps"; the gender mismatch "Bem-vindo ao *Computação Quântica na Prática*"; a missing preposition in "é essa a barreira que estamos nos aproximando"; and "new applications" rendered "novos aplicativos" (mobile-app sense) instead of "novas aplicações".

examples.source: Classical simulators … can make predictions about quantum mechanical systems. / his focus was on simulating quantum mechanical systems … a computer that operates according to a quantum mechanical description of the world
examples.suggested: …previsões sobre sistemas da mecânica quântica. / …simulação de sistemas da mecânica quântica … um computador que opera segundo uma descrição do mundo dada pela mecânica quântica
examples.translation: podem fazer previsões sobre sistemas quânticos mecânicos. / seu foco era na simulação de sistemas quânticos mecânicos … um computador que opera de acordo com uma descrição quântica mecânica do mundo
examples.why: "quantum mechanical" is a single compound adjective; splitting it yields "sistemas quânticos mecânicos" (= quantum systems that are mechanical) and "descrição quântica mecânica", which no Portuguese physicist writes. The next line of the same file uses the correct plain "sistemas quânticos", so the rendering is also inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: Proving impossibility results for classical computers is itself an impossibly difficult problem as far as we know.
examples.suggested: Provar resultados de impossibilidade para computadores clássicos é, em si, um problema absurdamente difícil, até onde sabemos.
examples.translation: Provar resultados de impossibilidade para computadores clássicos é, em si, um problema impossível, até onde sabemos.
examples.why: "impossibly difficult" (an intensifier meaning extremely hard) is strengthened to a flat "impossível", asserting the task cannot be done rather than that it is extraordinarily hard. The hedge "até onde sabemos" survives, so it stops short of misleading, but the claim is stronger than the English.

examples.source: essentially pulling physics and computational technology up by the bootstraps.
examples.suggested: essencialmente fazendo a física e a tecnologia computacional se impulsionarem mutuamente.
examples.translation: essencialmente elevando física e tecnologia computacional pelos próprios bootstraps.
examples.why: "bootstraps" is left in English inside a Portuguese sentence; the idiom does not exist in Portuguese, so the image is lost and the reader is left with an untranslated noun.

examples.source: Welcome to *Quantum Computing in Practice* … this is the wall we're approaching.
examples.suggested: Bem-vindo ao curso *Computação Quântica na Prática* … é dessa barreira que estamos nos aproximando.
examples.translation: Bem-vindo ao *Computação Quântica na Prática* … é essa a barreira que estamos nos aproximando.
examples.why: Two grammar slips a native editor would fix: "ao" clashes with the feminine title (needs "ao curso" or "à"), and "aproximar-se" requires the preposition "de" — "a barreira que estamos nos aproximando" is missing "da qual/de que".

examples.source: anyone that aims to develop new applications for quantum computers … T.J. Watson once famously predicted
examples.suggested: …desenvolver novas aplicações para computadores quânticos … T.J. Watson fez a célebre previsão de
examples.translation: qualquer pessoa que pretenda desenvolver novos aplicativos para computadores quânticos … T.J. Watson uma vez previu de forma famosa
examples.why: "aplicativos" means end-user apps (phone/desktop software), not "applications" in the sense of use cases for a technology — "aplicações" is the field's term, and the file itself uses "áreas de aplicação" later. "previu de forma famosa" is a word-for-word calque of "famously predicted" that no Portuguese writer would use.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the exception for classical computation, the independent-stochastic-noise setup, the "5 physical qubits per logical qubit / as if the 5-qubit code" caveat, the "logical qubits are *never* exposed" emphasis, and the closing break-even/threshold contrast ("ponto de equilíbrio" / "abaixo de um certo limiar") all land correctly, and the last 40% is the strongest part of the file. What a native editor would change is cosmetic: (1) the DefinitionTooltip for "entropia" still carries the English definition string ("Entropy is a measure of randomness…"), while the rest of the pt corpus translates these tooltips, so a hover shows English on an otherwise Portuguese page; (2) two calqued connectives — "Em hipótese, alguém poderia tentar desenvolver" for "Hypothetically speaking, one could attempt…" and the fragment "Talvez mais provável, poderiam existir erros localizados" for "Perhaps more likely, there could be errors…"; (3) "Outros modelos de ruído menos tolerantes" for "less forgiving" collides with "tolerante a falhas", the page's own key term, and reads ambiguously; and (4) "código de correção de erros quântico" puts the adjective where it appears to modify "erros" rather than "código". None of these mislead.

examples.source: <DefinitionTooltip definition="Entropy is a measure of randomness, uncertainty, or disorder in a system.">entropy</DefinitionTooltip>
examples.suggested: definition="A entropia é uma medida de aleatoriedade, incerteza ou desordem em um sistema."
examples.translation: <DefinitionTooltip definition="Entropy is a measure of randomness, uncertainty, or disorder in a system.">entropia</DefinitionTooltip>
examples.why: The tooltip body is user-visible prose and is rendered untranslated; every other DefinitionTooltip in the pt learning corpus (e.g. "O módulo é o resto após a divisão…") is translated, so this is an inconsistency the reader actually sees on hover.

examples.source: Hypothetically speaking, one could attempt to come up with a highly detailed, complicated noise model that aims to reflect the reality of what happens in a particular device.
examples.suggested: Hipoteticamente falando, seria possível tentar desenvolver um modelo de ruído bastante detalhado e complicado, que buscasse refletir a realidade do que acontece em um dispositivo específico.
examples.translation: Em hipótese, alguém poderia tentar desenvolver um modelo de ruído altamente detalhado e complicado que vise refletir a realidade do que acontece em um dispositivo específico.
examples.why: "Em hipótese" is not the idiomatic rendering of "hypothetically speaking", and the impersonal "one could" is better carried by "seria possível" than by the literal "alguém poderia"; reads as MT rather than as written Portuguese.

examples.source: Perhaps more likely, there could be errors that are localized but that nevertheless affect multiple components in a quantum computer.
examples.suggested: O que talvez seja mais provável: pode haver erros localizados que, ainda assim, afetam múltiplos componentes de um computador quântico.
examples.translation: Talvez mais provável, poderiam existir erros localizados, mas que mesmo assim afetam múltiplos componentes em um computador quântico.
examples.why: "Talvez mais provável," is a bare calque of the English adverbial fragment and is ungrammatical as a sentence-opening adjunct in Portuguese; a native writer would recast it with an adverb or a full clause.

examples.source: Other, less forgiving noise models are also commonly studied.
examples.suggested: Outros modelos de ruído menos indulgentes (mais severos) também são comumente estudados.
examples.translation: Outros modelos de ruído menos tolerantes também são comumente estudados.
examples.why: On a page whose subject is "tolerância a falhas", "menos tolerantes" invites the reading "models that tolerate less" rather than "models that are harsher on the implementation"; "menos indulgentes" or "mais severos" removes the collision with the page's own key term.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the delicate passages (fase global → vetor zero, "Isso é uma característica, não um bug!", "matrizes de densidade são sempre Hermitianas e portanto normais", semidefinida positiva, propriedade cíclica do traço) all land correctly, and terminology is correct and consistent (matriz de densidade, estado completamente misto, teorema espectral, decomposição espectral, autovalores/autovetores, base ortonormal). Three editorial slips: (1) "substituindo *quaisquer* dois vetores de estado de qubit ortogonais por $|0\rangle$ e $|1\rangle$" reverses the direction of the English "substituting any two orthogonal qubit state vectors for |0⟩ and |1⟩" — in PT "substituir X por Y" means replace X with Y, so the generalization reads backwards (the claim stays true because the situation is symmetric, hence MINOR, not FAIL); (2) a gender-agreement slip, "dado uma seleção aleatória" instead of "dada uma seleção aleatória"; (3) the calque "se deixarmos $A$ ser um vetor coluna" for "if we let A be a column vector", which a native technical writer would render as "se tomarmos $A$ como o vetor coluna". Informal register holds (implicit nós/você, no o senhor/vossa).

examples.source: In fact, we would again obtain the same result — the completely mixed state — by substituting *any* two orthogonal qubit state vectors for $\vert 0\rangle$ and $\vert 1\rangle.$
examples.suggested: Na verdade, obteríamos novamente o mesmo resultado — o estado completamente misto — substituindo $\vert 0\rangle$ e $\vert 1\rangle$ por *quaisquer* dois vetores de estado de qubit ortogonais.
examples.translation: Na verdade, obteríamos o mesmo resultado — o estado completamente misto — substituindo *quaisquer* dois vetores de estado de qubit ortogonais por $\vert 0\rangle$ e $\vert 1\rangle.$
examples.why: In Portuguese 'substituir X por Y' = replace X with Y, so the sentence says the arbitrary orthogonal pair is replaced BY |0>,|1> — the reverse of the English generalization. The claim remains true (the statement is symmetric), but the pedagogical direction 'this holds for any orthogonal pair' is inverted. 'again'/'novamente' is also dropped.

examples.source: We can verify that this makes sense by thinking about what we could hope to learn given a random selection of a state from one of the two possible state sets
examples.suggested: ... dada uma seleção aleatória de um estado de um dos dois possíveis conjuntos de estados
examples.translation: Podemos verificar que isso faz sentido pensando no que poderíamos esperar aprender dado uma seleção aleatória de um estado de um dos dois possíveis conjuntos de estados
examples.why: Gender-agreement error: 'seleção' is feminine, so it must be 'dada uma seleção', not 'dado uma seleção'. A native technical editor would fix this immediately.

examples.source: In particular, if we let $A$ be a column vector $\vert\phi\rangle$ and let $B$ be the row vector $\langle \phi\vert,$ then we see that
examples.suggested: Em particular, se tomarmos $A$ como o vetor coluna $\vert\phi\rangle$ e $B$ como o vetor linha $\langle \phi\vert,$ vemos que
examples.translation: Em particular, se deixarmos $A$ ser um vetor coluna $\vert\phi\rangle$ e $B$ ser o vetor linha $\langle \phi\vert,$ então vemos que
examples.why: 'deixarmos X ser' is a literal calque of English 'let X be'; Portuguese mathematical writing uses 'tomarmos X como' or 'seja X ...'. Grammatical but reads as machine translation.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or dropped caveats; quantities (127-qubit × 60-layer, 20 Trotter steps, 144 edges, three colors, ⟨Z_62⟩) and the ZNE/PEA and "data dependance" caveats all survive intact, and core terms (qubit, gate, coupling map, observable, transpile, backend, estimator) are kept in English consistently. What a native technical editor would change: two garbled non-words. "newly-defined `rzz`" is rendered twice as "bagong-taong `rzz`" (lines 139, 151), which reads as "new person/Bagong Taon", not "bagong-tukoy/bagong-tanging"; and "that quantum lead time" becomes "ang predwentahe ng quantum" (line 495), where "predwentahe" is not a Tagalog word at all (apparently a corruption of "bentahe"/"kalamangan"), and the "lead time" nuance is lost. Smaller slips: "logical equivalence" softened to "lohikal na pagkakatulad" (similarity, line 151); "for experimental simplicity" → "para sa kaginhawahan ng eksperimento" (convenience, line 44); the "partly because … partly because" construction is calqued as "bahagi dahil … bahagi dahil" with "kukuha ng mahabang panahon" for "will take … time" (line 52); and "Each laptop will be slightly different" drops the qualifier as "Magkakaiba-iba ang bawat laptop" (line 344). None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: Let us make a random use of the newly-defined `rzz`. / … our newly-defined `rzz` or `qc2` gate
examples.suggested: Subukan nating gamitin ang bagong-tukoy na `rzz`. / … ang bagong-tukoy nating `rzz` o `qc2` gate
examples.translation: Subukan nating gamitin ang bagong-taong `rzz`. / … ng ating bagong-taong `rzz` o `qc2` gate
examples.why: "bagong-taong" is not a Tagalog rendering of "newly-defined" — it parses as "new person" / evokes "Bagong Taon". Consistent but garbled; a native reader stumbles both times.

examples.source: …until at some point that quantum lead time becomes critically important.
examples.suggested: …hanggang sa puntong ang kalamangan sa oras (lead time) ng quantum ay nagiging kritikal na mahalaga.
examples.translation: …hanggang sa puntong ang predwentahe ng quantum ay nagiging kritikal na mahalaga.
examples.why: "predwentahe" is not a word in Tagalog (apparent corruption of "bentahe"/"kalamangan"), and "lead time" — the time head-start over classical reproduction — is flattened to a bare "advantage".

examples.source: let's verify the logical equivalence of `qc1` (the RZZ gate) for -pi/2 and our newly-defined `rzz`
examples.suggested: i-verify natin ang lohikal na pagkakapantay (equivalence) ng `qc1` …
examples.translation: i-verify natin ang lohikal na pagkakatulad ng `qc1` (ang RZZ gate) para sa -pi/2 at ng ating bagong-taong `rzz`
examples.why: `op1.equiv(op2)` returns exact operator equivalence, not mere similarity; "pagkakatulad" softens a strict equality claim into a resemblance.

examples.source: It took 161ms in wall time. Each laptop will be slightly different.
examples.suggested: …Bahagyang magkakaiba ang bawat laptop.
examples.translation: Tumagal ito ng 161ms sa wall time. Magkakaiba-iba ang bawat laptop.
examples.why: The qualifier "slightly" is dropped, so the reassurance that timings vary only a little reads as an unbounded "laptops all differ".

examples.source: partly because PEA is an experimental feature of Qiskit at this time of writing and partly because applying ZNE with PEA will take a fair amount of time.
examples.suggested: bahagyang dahil experimental pa ang PEA sa Qiskit sa panahon ng pagsulat nito, at bahagyang dahil matagal aabutin ang paggamit ng ZNE kasama ang PEA.
examples.translation: bahagi dahil ang PEA ay isang experimental na feature ng Qiskit sa oras ng pagsulat nito, at bahagi dahil ang paggamit ng ZNE na may PEA ay kukuha ng mahabang panahon.
examples.why: "bahagi dahil" is a word-for-word calque of "partly because", and "kukuha ng mahabang panahon" calques English "take time" (Tagalog uses "aabutin/tatagal").

editor_note: The bulk of the lesson is faithful and readable, but several precise technical statements are rendered with the wrong sense of a polysemous English word, and two of them state something the source does not. The Trotter section renders "for odd number of repetitions of the Trotter steps" as "para sa kakaibang bilang ng Trotter steps" ("for a strange/unusual number") — the actual rule (reverse ops on odd-numbered repetitions) is unrecoverable from the prose, and the file itself proves the right word was available, since Appendix I correctly writes "kung ang $r$ ay gansal". Section 1.3's disclaimer "We stop short of a rigorous proof of convergence behavior" becomes "Titigil tayo sa isang mahigpit na patunay ng gawi ng convergence", which reads as "we will stop AT a rigorous proof", i.e. promising the very thing the English declines to give. Secondary drift: "very large matrices" is three times "napakalalim na mga matrix" ("very DEEP matrices", lines ~149/196 and the fig-1 alt text) while sections 2/3/5 correctly say "napakalaking/napakalalaking matrix"; CG and GMRES are said to "limit" (Inililimitahan) rather than minimize the A-norm/residual norm, losing their defining optimality property; Appendix I says the evolutions are shifted "paataas" (upward) where the English says shifted backward; and "classically simulable phase shift" becomes "klasikal na maipapaliwanag" (classically explainable). Also worth a pass for lexical slips: "Itatalo natin na…" for "We will argue that", "nagsasara nang mahusay" for "converges efficiently" (vs. "nagco-converge" used elsewhere), and the non-words "masulbarang/sulbarang", "mapaghiwalatig", "mapansiyang".

examples.source: Furthermore, we reverse the order of the operations for odd number of repetitions of the Trotter steps, which is functionally equivalent but allows for synthesizing adjacent operations in a single $SU(2)$ unitary.
examples.suggested: …para sa gansal na bilang ng mga pag-ulit ng Trotter steps…
examples.translation: Bukod dito, bine-reverse natin ang pagkakasunod ng mga operasyon para sa kakaibang bilang ng Trotter steps, na katumbas sa functional na paraan ngunit nagpapahintulot ng pag-synthesize ng mga katabing operasyon sa isang $SU(2)$ unitary.
examples.why: "odd" (gansal) is rendered as "kakaiba" = strange/unusual. The stated condition is false and the real rule is unrecoverable from the prose; the same file correctly uses "gansal" for odd $r$ in Appendix I, so the split is also internally inconsistent.

examples.source: We stop short of a rigorous proof of convergence behavior.
examples.suggested: Hindi natin aabutin ang isang mahigpit na patunay ng gawi ng convergence.
examples.translation: Titigil tayo sa isang mahigpit na patunay ng gawi ng convergence.
examples.why: "Titigil tayo sa X" reads as "we will stop AT X", i.e. that a rigorous proof is provided — the opposite of the source's caveat that no rigorous proof is given.

examples.source: In problems involving very large matrices… / …eigenvalue/eigenvector problems of extremely large matrices. / An image showing a very large matrix being projected…
examples.suggested: napakalalaking mga matrix
examples.translation: Sa mga problemang may napakalalim na mga matrix… / …ng napakalalim na mga matrix. / Isang larawan na nagpapakita ng isang napakalalim na matrix…
examples.why: "malalim" = deep. Matrix SIZE is the whole premise of the lesson; sections 2, 3 and 5 correctly say "napakalaking/napakalalaking matrix", so section 1 both mistranslates and splits the term.

examples.source: It minimizes the A-norm of the error at each iteration… / It minimizes the residual norm over a Krylov space at each iteration…
examples.suggested: Mini-minimize / pinapaliit nito ang A-norm ng error… / …ang residual norm…
examples.translation: Inililimitahan nito ang A-norm ng error sa bawat iterasyon… / Inililimitahan nito ang residual norm sa isang Krylov space sa bawat iterasyon…
examples.why: "minimizes" softened to "limits". Minimization is the defining optimality property of CG and GMRES; "inililimitahan" only claims the quantity is bounded.

examples.source: that is, where all the time-evolutions are shifted backward by $d$ timesteps.
examples.suggested: …ay inilipat nang $d$ na timestep paatras.
examples.translation: iyon ay, kung saan ang lahat ng time-evolution ay inilipat ng $d$ na timestep paataas.
examples.why: "backward" becomes "paataas" (upward) — a wrong direction for the time shift that the appendix argument depends on.

examples.source: We will argue that… / the ground state error converges efficiently… / the classically simulable phase shift… / so that we can solve the generalized eigenvalue problem
examples.suggested: Mangangatwiran tayo na… / nagko-converge nang mahusay… / ang klasikal na masi-simulate na phase shift… / para malutas natin…
examples.translation: Itatalo natin na… / ang ground state error ay nagsasara nang mahusay… / ang klasikal na maipapaliwanag na phase shift… / para masulbarang natin ang generalized eigenvalue problem
examples.why: "argue"→"itatalo" (defeat), "converges"→"nagsasara" (closes; inconsistent with "nagco-converge" used elsewhere), "simulable"→"maipapaliwanag" (explainable), plus the non-words "masulbarang/sulbarang", "mapaghiwalatig", "mapansiyang" — machine-translation residue a native technical editor would rewrite.

editor_note: No hallucinations and no outright inverted claims — the ansatz/variational-form structure, the $D = 2^{2n}$ dimensionality argument, the three trade-offs (Bilis/Katumpakan/Ingay), and the N-local layer rules all survive intact, and the informal register holds throughout (no po/opo). What a native technical editor would fix is a cluster of ungrammatical focus/voice constructions that read as raw MT: "maaari kang subukan ng isang arbitrary na pamilya" (should be "maaari kang sumubok ng"/"maaari mong subukan ang"), "Maaari tayong ipasa ang ating mga data point" (should be "Maaari nating ipasa"), "Mayroon isang pundamental na trade-off" (missing linker: "Mayroong"), and "isang iba't ibang quantum state ang malilikha" ("iba't iba" = various, not "a different one"). Two word-level slips: "ilang mabait na mapping" renders "well-behaved mapping" with "mabait" (kind-hearted, of a person) instead of "maayos ang asal/kumikilos", and "pinaka-releban" is a malformed non-word for "pinakarelevante". Finally, "ang ika-0 qubit ay pinaka-malayo sa kanan" is ambiguous in Tagalog — the dominant reading is "farthest FROM the right", which risks teaching the opposite qubit ordering for the $ZZII$ string; "nasa pinakakanan" would be unambiguous. None of these rise to a false concept on their own, but together they are well past PASS.

examples.source: (recall that the 0th qubit is farthest right)
examples.suggested: (alalahanin na ang ika-0 qubit ang nasa pinakakanan)
examples.translation: (alalahanin na ang ika-0 qubit ay pinaka-malayo sa kanan)
examples.why: "Pinakamalayo sa kanan" most naturally parses as "farthest FROM the right", i.e. leftmost — the opposite of the source. This is the sentence that anchors Qiskit's little-endian ordering for $ZZII + IZZI + ...$, so an inverted reading would make the learner map the Z operators onto the wrong nodes.

examples.source: you can try an arbitrary family of parameterized circuits with fewer than $2^{2n}$ parameters
examples.suggested: maaari mong subukan ang isang arbitrary na pamilya ng mga parameterized circuit ...
examples.translation: maaari kang subukan ng isang arbitrary na pamilya ng mga parameterized circuit na may mas kaunti sa $2^{2n}$ na mga parameter
examples.why: "Maaari kang subukan ng X" is wrong focus — it reads as "you can be tried by X". Same defect at line 224 ("Maaari tayong ipasa ang ating mga data point" instead of "Maaari nating ipasa") and line 96 ("Mayroon isang" missing the -ng linker). Three instances of the same MT-grammar signature in one file.

examples.source: well-behaved mapping ... only the most relevant states are explored
examples.suggested: ilang mapping na maayos ang kilos (well-behaved) ... ang pinakarelevanteng mga estado lamang ang matuklas
examples.translation: ilang mabait na mapping ... ang pinaka-releban lamang na mga estado ang matuklas
examples.why: "Mabait" is the personal-character sense of kind/nice and is not used of a mathematical mapping; the technical sense of "well-behaved" is lost (only the parenthetical "tuluy-tuloy, differentiable" rescues it). "Pinaka-releban" is not a Tagalog word at all — the form is "relevante/relebante".

examples.source: Reducing the space could risk excluding the actual solution ... repeated alternatively one or more times ... solve a problem in a naive way
examples.suggested: ... panganib na hindi maisama/maiwan ang aktwal na solusyon ... paulit-ulit nang salitan isa o higit pang beses ... sa isang payak/naive na paraan
examples.translation: maaaring magdulot ng panganib na mailabas ang aktwal na solusyon ... paulit-ulit na alternately isa o higit pang beses ... malutas ang isang problema sa isang simpleng paraan
examples.why: "Mailabas" (to be brought out/released) is a weak stand-in for "excluding" and can be read as revealing rather than omitting the solution; "alternately" was left untranslated mid-sentence; and "naive" flattened to "simple", which drops the mildly pejorative sense that motivates the problem-specific ansaetze that follow.

editor_note: No misleading drift: every technical claim (SPMD/rank semantics, Sampler vs Estimator split, the four Qiskit-pattern stages, the SQD sequential-dependency argument, `--ntasks=4` requesting four classical tasks) matches the English, and the informal register holds throughout. What a native editor would fix is a cluster of malformed/wrong words and calques: the opening paragraph has the non-word "inuugos" (for "structured", should be "inaayos") and the malformed "inisakatuparan" (should be "isinasakatuparan"); the definition of parallel programming uses "naghahatid" ("delivers") where "naghahati" ("divides") is meant; and there are stray typos "madalay" (for "madalas", line ~88), "pinakadominate" (for "pinakadominante", line ~53), plus the ungrammatical "maaari kang maglalarawan" (line ~177) and "malutas ng mga makabuluhang problema" (should be "ang", line ~271). Two smaller calques: "Sa turn" for "In turn" (line ~170) and "Mayroon itong pamantayan na tinatawag na MPI" for "There is a standard called MPI" (line ~85, reads as "it has a standard"). Terminology is otherwise consistent and correct — qubit/gate/circuit/observable/transpilation kept in English, "expectation value" rendered as "expected value" consistently.

examples.source: Programming models are fundamental specifications that define how software is structured and executed.
examples.suggested: ... kung paano inaayos at isinasakatuparan ang software.
examples.translation: Ang mga modelo ng programming ay mga pangunahing espesipikasyon na nagtatakda kung paano inuugos at inisakatuparan ang software.
examples.why: "inuugos" is not a Tagalog word and "inisakatuparan" is malformed morphology; the very first sentence of the lesson reads as broken MT rather than as native technical prose.

examples.source: Parallel programming is a model that divides a program into sub-problems that can be executed simultaneously.
examples.suggested: ... isang modelo na naghahati ng isang programa sa mga sub-problema ...
examples.translation: Ang parallel programming ay isang modelo na naghahatid ng isang programa sa mga sub-problema na maaaring isagawa nang sabay-sabay.
examples.why: "naghahatid" means "delivers/transports", not "divides" — this is the definitional sentence of the section, so the core verb of the definition is the wrong word (concept still recoverable from context, hence minor).

examples.source: while a master process (often Rank 0) handles initialization and final aggregation
examples.suggested: habang ang isang master process (madalas ay Rank 0) ...
examples.translation: habang ang isang master process (madalay ay Rank 0) ang humahawak ng initialization at huling aggregation
examples.why: "madalay" is a typo for "madalas" ("often"); a native editor would catch it immediately in an otherwise careful bullet.

examples.source: In turn, we need the diagonalized matrix and the associated state vectors ...
examples.suggested: Kasunod nito, kailangan natin ang diagonalized na matrix ...
examples.translation: Sa turn, kailangan natin ang diagonalized na matrix at ang mga kaugnay na state vector ...
examples.why: "Sa turn" is a raw calque of the English discourse marker "in turn"; no Tagalog technical writer would write it, and idiomatic connectives exist.

examples.source: not necessarily a "rank" in the sense of prioritizing
examples.suggested: hindi naman kinakailangang "rank" sa diwa ng pagbibigay-prioridad
examples.translation: hindi nangangahulugang "rank" sa diwa ng pagbibigay-prioridad
examples.why: The hedge "necessarily" is dropped, turning a soft caveat into a flat denial. Non-misleading in practice here, but it is a strengthened claim relative to the English.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the load-bearing technical claims all survive intact (AES-256 "hanggang 9 rounds sa kabuuang 14 rounds ... security margin ... 5 rounds", Grover halving AES-128 "mula 128 bits sa 64 bits", the OTP "kung ang secret key ... ay maaaring secure na i-share, gayundin ang orihinal na plain text", "Wala sa dalawa ang kasalukuyang itinuturing na secure" for RC2/RC4), and register is consistently informal with no po/opo. What a native technical editor would change is phrasing, not substance: one clause is genuinely garbled — "sa pamamagitan ng pagpapahirap na hindi na magagawa sa computationally" for "by rendering them computationally infeasible" — and "obscuring the relationship" is rendered as "iniligaw ang relasyon" ("led astray"), where "itinatago/nililito ang relasyon" is the right verb. "Exchanged" in the TLS paragraph is rendered with "pinapalitan" ("is being replaced") twice — "ipinagpapalitan"/"ipinagpapalit" is the correct form; the concept is still recoverable from context, so this is imprecision rather than a false teaching. Smaller slips: "dapat tiyaking ang mga sumusunod na katangian" (should be "dapat tiyakin ang"), a missing "Ang" before "Security level ay isang sukatan", and "adopt/adoption" consistently rendered as "mag-angkop / pag-angkop" (adapt) instead of "mag-adopt / paggamit".

examples.source: Therefore, a large key space size provides resistance against brute force attacks by rendering them computationally infeasible.
examples.suggested: Kaya naman, ang malaking key space size ay nagbibigay ng proteksyon laban sa brute force attack dahil ginagawa nitong computationally infeasible ang mga ito.
examples.translation: Kaya naman, ang malaking key space size ay nagbibigay ng paglaban sa mga brute force attack sa pamamagitan ng pagpapahirap na hindi na magagawa sa computationally.
examples.why: "pagpapahirap na hindi na magagawa sa computationally" is not grammatical Tagalog — the English adverb is stranded after the preposition. Meaning is recoverable but the sentence reads as raw MT.

examples.source: ...obscuring the relationship between the ciphertext and the secret key.
examples.suggested: ...na itinatago ang relasyon sa pagitan ng ciphertext at ng secret key.
examples.translation: ...na iniligaw ang relasyon sa pagitan ng ciphertext at ng secret key.
examples.why: "iligaw" means to lead astray/lose, not to obscure or hide. The intended sense (the relationship is concealed) is only approximated, and the aspect marker is also wrong ("iniligaw" past vs. the surrounding present-habitual).

examples.source: ...the confidentiality and integrity of data exchanged between two parties. ... The key used in symmetric key encryption is securely exchanged using asymmetric key encryption...
examples.suggested: ...ng data na ipinagpapalitan ng dalawang partido. ... Ang key ... ay secure na ipinapadala/ipinagpapalit gamit ang asymmetric key encryption...
examples.translation: ...ang confidentiality at integrity ng data na pinapalitan ng dalawang partido. ... Ang key na ginagamit sa symmetric key encryption ay secure na pinapalitan gamit ang asymmetric key encryption...
examples.why: "pinapalitan" reads primarily as "is being replaced/substituted", not "is exchanged". In a key-exchange paragraph this nudges the learner toward "the symmetric key is replaced by asymmetric encryption" instead of "securely exchanged using it"; context still rescues it, hence minor.

examples.source: A symmetric key cryptosystem should ensure the following properties... / Security level is a measure of the difficulty of breaking a cipher...
examples.suggested: ...ay dapat tiyakin ang mga sumusunod na katangian... / Ang **security level** ay isang sukatan...
examples.translation: Ang isang symmetric key cryptosystem ay dapat tiyaking ang mga sumusunod na katangian... / **Security level** ay isang sukatan ng kahirapan ng pagbasag ng isang cipher...
examples.why: Two plain grammar slips a native writer would not make: "dapat tiyaking ang" (needs the infinitive "tiyakin"), and a definition sentence opening without the required "Ang" before the subject.

examples.source: ...with the adoption of quantum-safe products... / ...the ability of an information system to quickly and easily adopt alternative cryptographic primitives...
examples.suggested: ...ang pag-adopt/paggamit ng quantum-safe na mga produkto... / ...mabilis at madaling mag-adopt ng mga alternatibong cryptographic primitive...
examples.translation: ...ang pag-angkop ng quantum-safe na mga produkto... / ...mabilis at madaling mag-angkop ng mga alternatibong cryptographic primitive...
examples.why: "mag-angkop / pag-angkop" means to adapt or fit something, not to adopt/take into use. Used consistently for "adopt" in the crypto-agility section, where the point is precisely swapping in new primitives, not modifying them.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the quantities (0.74 Angstrom, -1.17 Hartrees, 500 optimization steps, resilience=1/TREX), the "for loop + variational trials are inside the session" note, and the final causal claim ("noise present in both cases, but error mitigation only on real hardware") all survive intact, and the informal natin/tayo register holds with no po/opo. The defects are surface: line 21 opens with the non-word "Ostaying sa ating pangunahing halimbawa" — an untranslated/garbled rendering of "Remaining with our basic example" that a native editor would immediately rewrite (e.g. "Mananatili tayo sa..."). Line 571 flattens the modal "That should be the inter-atomic distance found in nature" to a flat assertion "Iyon ang inter-atomic distance na makikita sa kalikasan" and calques "and indeed it is close" as "at katotohanan na malapit ito", which is not idiomatic Tagalog. Line 586 renders "The results ... are comparable" (i.e. similar in quality) as "ay maihahambing" (can be compared), and the title "Molecular na geometry" is a stiff English-adjective + na construction. None of these would cause a learner to form a false belief.

examples.source: Remaining with our basic example of diatomic hydrogen, the only geometric parameter to vary is the bond length.
examples.suggested: Mananatili tayo sa ating pangunahing halimbawa ng diatomic hydrogen; ang tanging geometric na parameter na babaguhin ay ang bond length.
examples.translation: Ostaying sa ating pangunahing halimbawa ng diatomic hydrogen, ang tanging geometric na parameter na babaguhin ay ang bond length.
examples.why: "Ostaying" is not a word in Tagalog or English — a leftover MT artifact from "Remaining". The sentence still parses from context, so it does not mislead, but it is the most visible non-native marker in the file.

examples.source: That should be the inter-atomic distance found in nature, and indeed it is close.
examples.suggested: Iyon dapat ang inter-atomic distance na makikita sa kalikasan, at tunay ngang malapit ito.
examples.translation: Iyon ang inter-atomic distance na makikita sa kalikasan, at katotohanan na malapit ito.
examples.why: "at katotohanan na malapit ito" is a word-for-word calque of "and indeed it is close" that no native technical writer would produce ("tunay ngang" is the idiom), and the modal "should be" is flattened into a bare assertion.

examples.source: The results from the real hardware are comparable, aside from a slightly different range of values sampled.
examples.suggested: Halos magkatulad ang mga resulta mula sa tunay na hardware, maliban sa bahagyang naiibang hanay ng mga halagang sinample.
examples.translation: Ang mga resulta mula sa tunay na hardware ay maihahambing, maliban sa bahagyang naiibang hanay ng mga halaga na sinample.
examples.why: Here "comparable" means "similar in quality", but "maihahambing" reads as "can be compared" — the evaluative point (results are about as good) is weakened to a bare statement of comparability.

examples.source: Molecular geometry / Determining a molecular geometry
examples.suggested: Geometriya ng molekula / Pagtukoy sa geometriya ng molekula
examples.translation: Molecular na geometry / Pagtukoy ng molecular na geometry
examples.why: The English-adjective + "na" + English-noun construction is stiff; the body text already uses "molekula" naturally (line 17), so the title is inconsistent with the prose's own convention.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the "ти" register holds; core terms are correct and consistent (анзац, спостережувана величина, дрейф пристрою, реальний час виконання for wall-clock, пом'якшення помилок used the same way in both the heading and the body). Three things a native technical editor would still change. First, the "unless" sentence at line 31 is rendered with the ambiguous conjunction "якщо тільки" over an inner negation ("якщо тільки … не всі вхідні дані готові"): the intended unless-reading is recoverable, but "якщо тільки" also reads as "only if", under which the sentence would advise the opposite default — "окрім випадків, коли…" removes the ambiguity. Second, line 17 drops the hedge in "which can help avoid drift" ("що допомагає уникнути дрейфу" asserts it flatly). Third, line 61 has "в виділеній сесії", violating the у/в euphony rule after a consonant. None of these misleads on its own in context, since lines 33–36 and 71 restate the batch-by-default recommendation explicitly.

examples.source: Generally, use batch mode unless you have workloads that don’t have all inputs ready at the outset.
examples.suggested: Загалом використовуй пакетний режим, окрім випадків, коли не всі вхідні дані готові з самого початку.
examples.translation: Загалом використовуй пакетний режим, якщо тільки у твоїх робочих навантаженнях не всі вхідні дані готові з самого початку.
examples.why: "якщо тільки" is doing double duty as "unless" on top of the clause's own "не всі"; read as "only if" (a common sense of the phrase) the sentence recommends batch precisely in the case the English excludes. The rest of the section keeps the reader on track, so this is a clarity risk rather than an outright inversion, but it is the one sentence in the file that should be reworded.

examples.source: There is usually minimal delay between jobs, which can help avoid drift.
examples.suggested: …, що може допомогти уникнути дрейфу.
examples.translation: Зазвичай затримка між завданнями мінімальна, що допомагає уникнути дрейфу.
examples.why: The modal "can" is dropped, turning a hedged benefit into a flat guarantee that batch mode avoids drift.

examples.source: …apply it to subsequent jobs when running in dedicated session.
examples.suggested: …застосовувати її до наступних завдань під час роботи у виділеній сесії.
examples.translation: …застосовувати її до наступних завдань при роботі в виділеній сесії.
examples.why: "в виділеній" breaks the у/в euphony rule after a consonant; "при роботі" is also a calqued nominalization where "під час роботи" is what a Ukrainian technical writer would use.

editor_note: The prose is faithful, natural and informal throughout ("ти"-form: «Використовуй `qasm2.loads()`…», «Ти можеш вказати імпортеру…»), and core terms are consistent (gate→вентиль, circuit→схема, qubit→кубіт, importer/exporter→імпортер/експортер). Three things a native technical editor would change. (1) A stray untranslated English bullet «- Review the [Verify your program](/guides/debugging-tools) topic.» is spliced in right after the "Докладніше — у довіднику…" line at the top of the "Імпорт програми OpenQASM 2 у Qiskit" section; it belongs only to the "Наступні кроки" list at the end (where it correctly appears as «Ознайомся з темою [Перевірка програми]») and should simply be deleted from line 52. (2) "basis gates" is rendered «базові вентилі» (base/basic gates) rather than the conventional «базисні вентилі». (3) In the first warning admonition, "the default settings of the importer might not be able to import a program exported by our exporter" is softened to «можуть не розпізнати програму» (might not recognize), which loses the concrete "fail to import" claim.

examples.source: (no corresponding source text at this position — the line belongs to the "Next steps" list: "- Review the [Verify your program](/guides/debugging-tools) topic.")
examples.suggested: (delete the line — it is already correctly translated at the end as «Ознайомся з темою [Перевірка програми](./debugging-tools).»)
examples.translation: - Review the [Verify your program](/guides/debugging-tools) topic.
examples.why: An untranslated English bullet from the closing Recommendations list has been injected mid-document, immediately after «Докладніше — у довіднику [OpenQASM 2 Qiskit API]…» and before the «### Імпорт простих програм» heading. It is content the source does not have at that point, it breaks the section flow, and it is the one piece of raw English left in the prose.

examples.source: certain other quantum platforms that treat the "basis gates" of their hardware as built-in instructions
examples.suggested: …які вважають «базисні вентилі» свого обладнання вбудованими інструкціями
examples.translation: деякими іншими квантовими платформами, які вважають «базові вентилі» свого апаратного забезпечення вбудованими інструкціями
examples.why: "Basis gates" is a fixed term for the hardware's native gate basis; «базові» reads as "basic/base gates", while the established Ukrainian rendering is «базисні вентилі». Recognizable but imprecise.

examples.source: This means that the default settings of the importer might not be able to import a program exported by our importer.
examples.suggested: Це означає, що зі стандартними налаштуваннями імпортер може виявитися неспроможним імпортувати програму, експортовану нашим експортером.
examples.translation: Це означає, що стандартні налаштування імпортера можуть не розпізнати програму, експортовану нашим експортером.
examples.why: "might not be able to import" is a hard failure to load the program; «можуть не розпізнати» softens it to "might not recognize", which a learner could read as a cosmetic warning rather than an import error. (The translation does correctly repair the English source's own importer/exporter typo.)

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats; the monitoring → calibration → benchmarking chain, the "modest vs severe TLS activity" contrast, "менше двох годин на день", and the queue-pause caveat all track the English, and the informal "ти можеш"/"натисни" register holds. Four editorial slips remain. (1) "single-qubit gates: sx, x, rx" is rendered "одиночних квантових воріт" ("single quantum gates"), which drops the "qubit" in the term — the heading "Операції з одиночними кубітами" rescues it, but the sentence alone teaches the wrong compound. (2) "по ураженим кубітам" is a Russified dative after "по"; Ukrainian requires the locative "по уражених кубітах" (and "уражені" reads as "damaged" rather than merely "affected"). (3) "non-nearest-neighbor qubits" → "ненайближчих сусідніх кубітів" is a stacked calque a native writer would rephrase as "кубітів, які не є найближчими сусідами". (4) EPLG's "100-qubit length string" (a chain/path of qubits) becomes "рядка довжиною 100 кубітів", where "рядок" reads as a text line/row rather than "ланцюжок". "Ворота" for gate is used consistently and is left as a defensible house convention.

examples.source: These calibrations ensure accurate implementation of the single-qubit gates: sx, x, rx (fractional).
examples.suggested: Ці калібрування забезпечують точну реалізацію однокубітних воріт: sx, x, rx (дробові).
examples.translation: Ці калібрування забезпечують точну реалізацію одиночних квантових воріт: sx, x, rx (дробові).
examples.why: "одиночних квантових воріт" means "single quantum gates", losing the qubit-count sense of "single-qubit"; the file elsewhere uses "двокубітні" for two-qubit, so "однокубітних" is both correct and internally consistent.

examples.source: These calibrations are batched across the affected qubits and executed concurrently where appropriate
examples.suggested: Ці калібрування групуються в пакети по задіяних кубітах і виконуються паралельно там, де це доцільно
examples.translation: Ці калібрування пакетуються по ураженим кубітам і виконуються паралельно там, де це доцільно
examples.why: "по" governs the locative in Ukrainian ("по кубітах", not "по кубітам") — the dative here is a Russianism; "уражені" also connotes "damaged" rather than the neutral "affected/concerned".

examples.source: These calibrations are run in batches of non-nearest-neighbor qubits to minimize crosstalk.
examples.suggested: Ці калібрування виконуються пакетами з кубітів, які не є найближчими сусідами, щоб мінімізувати перехресні завади.
examples.translation: Ці калібрування виконуються пакетами ненайближчих сусідніх кубітів для мінімізації перехресних завад.
examples.why: "ненайближчих сусідніх" is a stacked calque of the English hyphenated modifier; no Ukrainian technical writer would coin "ненайближчий", and the relative clause reads naturally.

examples.source: Layer fidelity (EPLG), for the best 100-qubit length string
examples.suggested: Точність шару (EPLG) для найкращого ланцюжка довжиною 100 кубітів
examples.translation: Точність шару (EPLG) для найкращого рядка довжиною 100 кубітів
examples.why: EPLG is reported over a connected chain/path of qubits; "рядок" primarily means a line of text or a table row in Ukrainian technical usage, while "ланцюжок" is the established rendering for a qubit chain.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — dates, quantities (68 нс проти 138 нс, 2.15e-3 на 100 кубітах, 20-2000 µs, 2 477 кубітів на 17 QPU), conditions and caveats all survive, and informal "ти" holds with zero Ви/Ваш slips. What a native technical editor would fix: (1) the recurring ungrammatical "зверни до [документації/цих інструкцій]" — six times (lines 120, 126, 134, 150, 220, 329); the reflexive "звернися до" is required, "зверни" alone means "turn something". (2) "Classical feedforward and control flow" is rendered "Класичний зворотний зв'язок та управління потоком" (line 466) — feedforward is turned into its opposite, feedback; better "класичний прямий зв'язок (feedforward)". (3) "Log 20 minutes of compute in any 12-month period" becomes "Заходь на 20 хвилин обчислень…" (line 89) = "drop by for 20 minutes", the wrong sense of "log"; "Наробиш 20 хвилин обчислень" / "Використай 20 хвилин обчислень" is the intent. (4) "preview service" is rendered "попередній сервіс" (lines 29, 97) = "the previous service", while the same word is handled correctly as "попередній перегляд" for the Qiskit Functions preview at line 642. (5) "engine stack" → "стек двигуна" (lines 479, 492) is a calque — "рушій" not "двигун". (6) "fault-tolerant" is split within the file: "квантових обчисленнях з виправленням помилок" at line 401 vs "відмовостійкої транспіляції / відмовостійких цілей" at line 403. None of these would make a learner form a false belief about the platform updates being announced.

examples.source: See [Classical feedforward and control flow](/guides/classical-feedforward-and-control-flow) and [Deferred timing resolution using stretch](/guides/stretch) for more information and code examples.
examples.suggested: Дивися [Класичний прямий зв'язок (feedforward) та управління потоком](…) та [Відкладене визначення таймінгу за допомогою stretch](…)
examples.translation: Дивися [Класичний зворотний зв'язок та управління потоком](/guides/classical-feedforward-and-control-flow) та [Відкладене вирішення таймінгу за допомогою розтягування](/guides/stretch) …
examples.why: "feedforward" is rendered as "зворотний зв'язок" = feedback, the directional opposite; the source itself distinguishes feedback (line 51, correctly translated "логіка зворотного зв'язку") from the feedforward guide title. Also "вирішення таймінгу" is a calque of "resolution" in the wrong sense (settlement vs determination) — "визначення таймінгу".

examples.source: For guidance on retrieving data from past jobs, refer to the following documentation.
examples.suggested: Щоб дізнатися, як отримати дані з попередніх завдань, звернися до цієї документації.
examples.translation: Щоб отримати вказівки з отримання даних про попередні завдання, зверни до такої документації.
examples.why: "зверни до" is ungrammatical — the verb needs the reflexive form "звернися до"; as written it reads as "turn [something] to". It recurs six times, so it is a systematic slip, not a typo. The doubled "отримати вказівки з отримання" in the same sentence is also clumsy.

examples.source: Log 20 minutes of compute in any 12-month period and you can opt in to a special one-time offer: 180 minutes for the next 12 months.
examples.suggested: Використай 20 хвилин обчислень протягом будь-якого 12-місячного періоду — і зможеш підписатися на спеціальну одноразову пропозицію: 180 хвилин на наступні 12 місяців.
examples.translation: Заходь на 20 хвилин обчислень у будь-який 12-місячний період і ти зможеш скористатися спеціальною одноразовою пропозицією: 180 хвилин на наступні 12 місяців.
examples.why: "Log" here means accumulate/record usage, not "log in" or "drop by"; "Заходь на 20 хвилин" reads as an invitation to visit for 20 minutes. The eligibility quantity survives, so this is a wrong verb sense rather than a misleading condition.

examples.source: Qiskit Code Assistant service discontinued - The preview service has been discontinued and the Visual Studio Code and JupyterLab extensions have been archived.
examples.suggested: …— сервіс у режимі попереднього перегляду (preview) припинено…
examples.translation: Сервіс Qiskit Code Assistant припинено — попередній сервіс було припинено, а розширення для Visual Studio Code і JupyterLab архівовано.
examples.why: "попередній сервіс" reads as "the previous service", not "the preview service". The file itself uses the correct "попередній перегляд" for the Qiskit Functions preview at line 642, so the rendering is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: unlocking compilation to Pauli-based computation - a common representation in fault-tolerant quantum computing … Improvements in early fault-tolerant transpilation
examples.suggested: Use "відмовостійкі квантові обчислення" in both places.
examples.translation: …відкриваючи можливість компіляції для обчислень на основі Паулі — поширеного представлення в квантових обчисленнях з виправленням помилок … Вдосконалення ранньої відмовостійкої транспіляції
examples.why: "fault-tolerant" is rendered two different ways two lines apart — "з виправленням помилок" (error-correcting) and "відмовостійкий". The first also narrows the concept: error correction is a means, fault tolerance the property. The concept stays identifiable, so this is inconsistency rather than a false teaching.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, the T2 ≤ 2·T1 caveat, the qubit-order caveat for [0,1] vs [1,0], and the readout-error A/B (recorded vs true bit) definitions all survive intact, and informal "ти" holds consistently. Three fixable things: (1) a stray, untranslated English bullet is spliced in at line 34, immediately after the package-versions accordion and before the intro paragraph — it is a duplicate of the "Next steps" recommendation that also correctly appears (translated) at line 548, so the page opens with an orphan English link that has no source counterpart there; it should simply be deleted. (2) "noisy" is rendered three different ways within the file: «галасливий» (lines 35, 65 — the everyday word for "loud/rowdy", wrong register for a physics text), "зашумлена" (lines 426, 523) and "симуляція з шумом" (lines 4, 343); "зашумлений" is the correct domain choice and should be used throughout. (3) "bit-flip" splits between "перевертання біту" (line 113) and "перекидання бітів"/"перекинути" (lines 388, 392, 395). Also cosmetic: "одно-кубітна"/"дво-кубітного" are hyphenated where Ukrainian orthography wants "однокубітна"/"двокубітного".

examples.source: (no counterpart at this position — the English intro paragraph follows the accordion directly)
examples.suggested: delete the line entirely (it already exists, translated, at line 548 under «Наступні кроки»)
examples.translation: - To simulate noisy circuits, see [Exact and noisy simulation with Qiskit Aer primitives](/guides/simulate-with-qiskit-sdk-primitives).
examples.why: An untranslated English bullet from the Next-steps block is spliced into the top of the page where the source has nothing. It is not a false statement, but it is content that does not belong at that position and it breaks the page's opening.

examples.source: This is useful for emulating noisy quantum processors … / stores a noise model used for noisy simulation
examples.suggested: емуляції зашумлених квантових процесорів … / під час зашумленої симуляції
examples.translation: корисно для емуляції «галасливих» квантових процесорів … / під час «галасливої» симуляції
examples.why: «Галасливий» means noisy in the acoustic/rowdy sense; the scare quotes show the translator felt it was off. The rest of the file already uses «зашумлений» (lines 426, 523), so this is both a wrong-register term and a within-file split.

examples.source: To construct a 5% single-qubit bit-flip error / flip the state of the qubit
examples.suggested: pick one — «перекидання біта» / «перекинути» — and use it in all four places
examples.translation: помилки перевертання біту (113) vs «помилками перекидання бітів» / «перекинути стан кубіта» (388, 392)
examples.why: The same core concept (bit-flip) is named two ways within one page; recognizable, but a native technical editor would unify it.

examples.source: That suggests you should write your own transpiler pass … if you need to insert your quantum errors
examples.suggested: Отже, варто написати власний прохід транспілятора …
examples.translation: Це означає, що тобі потрібно написати власний transpiler pass …
examples.why: «That suggests you should» is advisory; «це означає, що тобі потрібно» states a requirement. The conditional clause at the end keeps it from misleading, but the hedge is flattened.

editor_note: Overall faithful, consistently informal (ти: «Відкрий», «Знайди», «твоєму обліковому записі»), and terminologically stable (instance→інстанс, workload→робоче навантаження, QPU kept, job→завдання). Three things a native technical editor would change. (1) In the currency Admonition the comparison is garbled: the English contrasts ONE amount at two moments (USD calculation vs. actual local-currency charge), while the Ukrainian «може відрізнятися від суми, початково розрахованої в USD, та від суми, яку фактично стягнуть» makes the cost differ from BOTH amounts, implying a nonexistent third quantity; the practical takeaway survives only because the next sentence restates it. (2) Same paragraph has a case error, «тебе стягують плату» instead of «з тебе стягують плату». (3) The normative «must be used with other methods of cost management» is softened to «слід використовувати», i.e. a recommendation rather than a requirement.

examples.source: Because currency exchange rates can fluctuate, the cost for X runtime seconds might be different when initially calculated in USD than when you’re actually charged in your local currency.
examples.suggested: Оскільки обмінні курси можуть коливатися, вартість X секунд виконання, початково розрахована в USD, може відрізнятися від суми, яку фактично стягнуть з тебе в місцевій валюті.
examples.translation: Оскільки обмінні курси можуть коливатися, вартість X секунд виконання може відрізнятися від суми, початково розрахованої в USD, та від суми, яку фактично стягнуть у місцевій валюті.
examples.why: The English compares one amount at two points in time (USD calculation vs. actual local-currency charge). The Ukrainian turns it into a comparison against two separate amounts, so it reads as if there were a third, distinct 'cost' — an incoherent claim the source does not make.

examples.source: However, for monthly billing purposes, you are charged in your local currency, specified on your IBM Cloud account.
examples.suggested: Однак для щомісячного виставлення рахунків з тебе стягують плату в місцевій валюті, указаній у твоєму обліковому записі IBM Cloud.
examples.translation: Однак для щомісячного виставлення рахунків тебе стягують плату в місцевій валюті, яка вказана у твоєму обліковому записі IBM Cloud.
examples.why: «стягувати плату» governs «з когось», not the accusative — «тебе стягують плату» is ungrammatical and no native technical writer would leave it.

examples.source: IBM Cloud spending notifications must be used with other methods of cost management for several reasons:
examples.suggested: Сповіщення про витрати IBM Cloud обов'язково потрібно використовувати разом з іншими методами керування витратами з кількох причин:
examples.translation: Сповіщення про витрати IBM Cloud слід використовувати разом з іншими методами управління витратами з кількох причин:
examples.why: «слід» downgrades a hard requirement ('must') to advice; the whole point of the bullet list that follows is that notifications alone are insufficient. Also note «управління витратами» here vs «керування витратами» in the title — a small internal inconsistency.
